changes: Pooled Tables 2 and 3 over FY1994–2005 (original FY1994–2000 plus FY2001–2005). Pooled Table 4 over FY1994–2004 (original FY1994–1999 plus FY2000–2004), retaining the accepted one-year future-sales lead. The paper's general sample description is 1994–2000; the accepted Table 4 code's narrower fit window controls those rows.

Extended the accepted source bounds to match the pooled windows: Compustat FY1992–2006; historical price keys FY1993–2004 and monthly/daily price dates through 31 Dec 2005; exchange rates and IBES fiscal-period years through 2006. The accepted GVKEY/fiscal-year uniqueness assertion passed on the extended Compustat screen.

Kept the source construction and estimators, including currency handling, lag/lead rules, target screens, calibration fits, and probit terms. Added aggregate coverage summaries and active e(sample) counts on the retained numeric fyear field. A final added esttab artifact export was placed after est clear; this caused each selected Stata cell to end with r(111), despite its probit, counts, and four standard aggregate exports having completed.
limitations: The one controller launch produced a successful SAS build and handoff, but all eight eligible Stata cells are marked unsuccessful: each printed its EXT_SAMPLE counts and wrote the standard result files, then the added artifact export after est clear failed with r(111), ‘estimation result m1 not found.’ The receipt has no successful-cell proofs. In keeping with the single-launch instruction, no retry was made; none of these scopes receives extension credit or a report artifact. Counts and coefficients in each row's reason/comparison are diagnostic-only outputs from the failed cell.

Table 2 target 2 remains prior_unexecuted because the assigned predecessor has no valid estimate: its corrected handoff ran (3,144 rows; 3,128 after perfect-prediction deletions), but Stata failed to converge after 300 iterations (r(430)); SIC2 14/45/75 lost 1/11/4 rows, and Stata reported 48 failures and 41 successes completely determined. No valid exports were retained and the task assigns no eligible cell for replay.

Table 4's paper-wide sample description says 1994–2000, but the accepted FL construction and handoff end at FY1999 because the model uses next-year sales. The replay preserves the accepted Table 4 endpoint and adds FY2000–2004; this differs from the requested 2005 endpoint for Tables 2 and 3 by design.

Current local data files are later vintages than the study's 1990s source data. The provider guide supports the legacy Compustat item crosswalk, but current-vintage equivalence to the paper's vendor snapshot, IBES historical links, and exact forecast-period conventions is not established. No unavailable component was imputed.

The paper's IBES stock-split adjustment-factor-above-3 screen is unavailable in the selected summary/detail files and was not substituted from another field. Ticker/PERMNO/GVKEY matching, unique-link exclusions, and the 62-day IBES-to-Compustat date tolerance remain documented best-effort construction choices.

The accepted construction follows the explicit p.504 DTE percentile narrative and leaves unresolved the Table 1 p.511 note that also describes percentile trimming on accrual measures; the target-specific DTE percentile population is also not specified by the paper. It follows the primary-table t−1 market-equity note for EM1 despite Table 1's t−2 definition.

The paper does not specify a probit covariance estimator; Stata's model-based covariance remains in use. The paper's narrative calls p-values one-tailed while Table 2 labels them ‘Prob > chi-square’; the accepted two-sided export convention is retained.

The source/sample-size records and predecessor exports are not fully aligned: the assigned sample record reports 4,139 for the Table 2 main sample while the predecessor Table2_T1 export reports 4,995 observations; the accepted design also records a Table 4 analyst-sample count discrepancy. No screens were changed to force agreement. In FY2004 price-key support, 622 historical price currencies remained unresolved after accepted verification rules and therefore stay missing.
